summary: All five targeted hypotheses confirmed. ECON-001 (under-distribution / path-dependence), ECON-003 (phUSD over-mint), and CODE-002/M-01 (stale-debt underflow brick) reproduce under forge invariant, forge deterministic property tests, AND Medusa. INV-1 (totalStaked==sum), INV-3 (stable solvency), accumulator monotonicity and lastRewardTime monotonicity hold across 128k calls/invariant in forge and 2.0M calls in Medusa.

confirmedFindings.title: Linear Depletion pays out as exponential decay; under-distribution is path-dependent on poke count

counterexample.property: distribution over one depletionDuration must be ~100% and independent of interaction cadence
minimalSequence: loop N times over depletionDuration: warp(D/N); claim()  (poke without funding)
counterexample.result: N=2 distributes 74.99% (B0*(1-(1-1/N)^N)); N->inf distributes 63.2% (B(t)=B0*e^(-t/D)). 1 poke distributes ~100%, proving the realized rate is controlled by whoever pokes the pool.

confirmedFindings.title: pause -> pauseWithdraw -> unpause over-mints phUSD (stale phUSDPerSecond + frozen lastRewardTime)

counterexample.property: reward phUSD minted to a staker (and globally) must not exceed the APY-implied cap stake*APY*time

medusa.observed: property_no_over_mint() returned false (rewardMinted exceeds fair APY integral)

confirmedFindings.title: Partial pauseWithdraw leaves reward debt anchored to the larger pre-withdraw amount -> claim/withdraw/stake underflow-revert (account brick)

counterexample.property: a staker who did a PARTIAL pauseWithdraw must still be able to claim/withdraw after unpause without revert

sequence: collectReward(100000e18); warp(7d); alice claim()  (anchors stableDebt at 1000e18 * accStable / PRECISION)
alice pauseWithdraw(500e18)  (amount -> 500e18, stableDebt still sized for 1000e18)
deterministicPoC.result: claim() and withdraw() revert with arithmetic underflow; remaining 500e18 principal recoverable ONLY via re-pause + pauseWithdraw
